fixes.explanation: That's right, baker. In the song, God says to Jacob and Israel, ‘I will give you the land of Canaan as the portion of your inheritance.’ (1 Chronicles 16:18) It's a promise made as an inheritance. Notice it's land, not a thing you can put in your pocket.

Not just the Levites, friend. The text says David distributed a loaf of bread, a date cake and a raisin cake to every man and woman of Israel (1 Chronicles 16:3). The Levites weren't the only ones getting a snack. Every man and woman of Israel was on that list.

That's right, it's FALSE. David gave a loaf of bread, a date cake and a raisin cake to every man and woman of Israel (1 Chronicles 16:3). The list wasn't just the Levites. That's how you throw a celebration.

This one is actually true, friend. The song says, “let the hearts of those who seek the LORD rejoice.” (1 Chronicles 16:10) I know, it sounded too easy to be true. I second-guess the easy ones myself, so no shame here.

Kings is right. The song says of the LORD, “He rebuked kings on their behalf…” (1 Chronicles 16:21). Then the LORD says, ‘Do not touch My anointed ones! Do no harm to My prophets!’ (1 Chronicles 16:22) Even kings got told to keep their hands to themselves.

Elders aren't the ones in this verse. It says, “He rebuked kings on their behalf…” (1 Chronicles 16:21). Then the LORD says, ‘Do not touch My anointed ones! Do no harm to My prophets!’ (1 Chronicles 16:22). The word you're looking for is kings.

That's the reason the song gives. “For all the gods of the nations are idols, but it is the LORD who made the heavens.” (1 Chronicles 16:26) On one side, idols. On the other, the One who made the heavens. That's a big gap, friend.

Idols aren't what the song says to bring. Just a few verses earlier it says, “For all the gods of the nations are idols…” (1 Chronicles 16:26). What it tells them to bring is, “bring an offering and come before Him.” (1 Chronicles 16:29) The thing it names is an offering, friend.

No swords in this invitation, friend. The song says, “bring an offering and come before Him.” (1 Chronicles 16:29) A sword would be a strange thing to carry into my bakery, and I'd have questions. The thing the song names to bring is an offering.

That's the reason in the song. “Then the trees of the forest will sing for joy before the LORD, for He is coming to judge the earth.” (1 Chronicles 16:33) The reason given is His coming. No tricks in this one, baker, you read it right.

This one is actually true, friend. The song says, “Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; His loving devotion endures forever.” (1 Chronicles 16:34) Earlier the song just said to give thanks (1 Chronicles 16:8), and this time it comes with the reason. A line that familiar is easy to second-guess, and I won't hold it against you.

Ruling isn't in this cry, friend. It says, “…that we may give thanks to Your holy name, that we may glory in Your praise.” (1 Chronicles 16:35) The reason given is thanks and praise. The people ask to be saved so they can give thanks, not so they can take over.

This one is actually true, friend. After the song, all the people said, “Amen!” and “Praise the LORD!” (1 Chronicles 16:36) The whole crowd answered together. I'd have been hollering right along with them, so don't sweat this one.
